text:
maria: Quick sync — replay harness is showing a ~12% tail latency regression after the kernel selection change we pushed yesterday. I ran an apples-to-apples replayer run against the same scrubbed cohort and the numbers diverge. Can we do a determinism + parity audit?

ken: Got the baseline vs new run. Baseline p95=220ms p99=480ms, new p95=248ms p99=540ms. Throughput slightly lower too (~6%). Logs attached in the run dir: s3://replay-logs/2536009876/bench_summary.txt

ash: Two quick hypotheses: 1) sampling or cohort differences (seed/assignment), 2) KV cache warmup/eviction behavior changed because kernel configuration altered batching alignment.

nina: +1 on KV. After the kernel change we changed micro-batching padding (pad to 32 vs pad to 16) which can reorder batch packing. That can change the order of KV insertions and therefore eviction order (we currently use LRU with timestamp tie-breakers). Small reorder -> different cache hit distribution -> different effective prefix lengths -> latency change.

maria: Do we have per-run KV hit traces? I remember we added a small CSV export in the replayer.

ken: Yep, here are the KV metrics from both runs (snippet):
```
run: baseline
kv_hits: 37421
kv_misses: 12834
kv_hit_rate: 0.744
avg_latency_ms: 210

run: kernel-change
kv_hits: 34512
kv_misses: 15745
kv_hit_rate: 0.686
avg_latency_ms: 226
```

ash: That's a pretty clear hit-rate delta. Two follow-ups: 1) confirm replayer determinism (same seed, same sharding), 2) recreate the kernel selection table inside the replayer so it picks the same kernels as prod. If replayer picks a different execution path we'll see different memory layout/packing.

maria: How do we force the kernel table? Is there an env flag?

nina: We put an override in runtime last quarter: `KERNEL_OVERRIDES=/etc/runtime/kernel_table.json` — if you mount the exact prod kernel_table.json into the replayer container it will mimic selection. Also set `REPLAYER_SEED=<commit-hash-salted>` to match cohort shard mapping.

eva: Also recommend a deterministic KV prewarm step so replayed traces don't depend on ordering heuristics. Recipe I used for other parity checks: 1) extract top 10k prefixes by frequency 2) replay those prefixes in deterministic order to fill the KV store 3) run the actual replay. Command: 
```bash
# generate ordered prefix file
python tools/prefix_extract.py --trace s3://prod-scrubbed/cohort.tgz --top 10000 --out prefixes.txt --seed 42
# prewarm
./replayer --mode prewarm --prefix-file prefixes.txt --kv-endpoint $KV_URL
# run main
./replayer --mode replay --cohort cohort.json --seed 42 --kernel-override /mnt/prod_kernel_table.json
```

maria: Nice. That should eliminate warmup variance. Can we also add an assertion in the replayer that emits the kernel table hash used in the run (so we can signal mismatches automatically)?

ken: I can add that check. Plan: run prewarm+replay with kernel override + same seed, then compare KV hit CSVs. If hit rates diverge >1% we mark parity-fail and attach artifacts.

sre-bot: perf-checker job queued: job_id=perf-2536009876. Will post results to thread when complete. :gear:

nina: One more gotcha — the new kernel changed the internal ordering of batches in the op scheduler, and our LRU timestamps use monotonic clock per-thread. For deterministic eviction across runs, we need a sequence counter incremented from the replayer (not per-thread time). Otherwise thread scheduling differences produce eviction ties.

ash: Good catch. We should add a deterministic eviction mode `KV_EVICTION_MODE=deterministic_sequence` that uses a global counter injected by the replayer during prewarm/replay. That should lock down ordering.

maria: OK action items: (1) ken: run prewarm+replay with kernel override and same seed, (2) ash/nina: prototype deterministic eviction mode, (3) eva: share prefix extraction script + small README, (4) add kernel-table-hash logging to replayer. I'll own the parity gating rule (1% hit-rate threshold).

ken: Starting the run now. ETA ~30m.

maria: Thanks all. If this repros we can triage whether to revert padding change or keep change and add deterministic prewarm in CI. :thumbsup:
